researchSummary.finding: Dyfi Bike Park is a real, active, verified operator. The company DYFI BIKE PARK LIMITED (Companies House No. 10605938, active) operates a 650-acre gravity mountain bike park in Esgair Forest near Pantperthog, Machynlleth, Mid Wales. Core contact details (website, phone, email, address), company registration, trail descriptions, facilities, opening hours, and indicative pricing have all been sourced from official/recognised directories. The main outstanding gaps are: (1) no logo image with a free licence; (2) no premium cover image with a free licence — only one low-quality Geograph photo exists under CC BY-SA 2.0; (3) the official website (dyfibikepark.co.uk) returns HTTP 403 for all pages, preventing direct verification of current pricing and the full trail count; (4) no verified Google rating.

description.short: A 650-acre gravity mountain bike park in Esgair Forest near Machynlleth, hand-crafted by World Cup-winning rider Dan Atherton. Trails range from red to triple black diamond, with Land Rover uplift, a café, and a bike shop.
description.shortNote: Derived from verified third-party sources (MBWales, Visit Mid Wales, ibikeride.com, MBUK). No AI-generated content used.
description.full: Dyfi Bike Park sits within 650 acres of Esgair Forest, three miles north of Machynlleth in Mid Wales, on the southern border of Snowdonia National Park. The park was conceived and hand-built by Dan Atherton — World Cup winner and one of mountain biking's most celebrated riders — who purchased the forest and relocated on-site to oversee construction personally. The park opened to the public in summer 2019 and has since expanded to 18 tracks across two mountain sections (Upper and Lower). Trails range from red-grade (intermediate) to triple black diamond (pro-level), with the longest descents exceeding 3.5km and 400m of vertical drop. An uplift service using Land Rovers runs 10am–4pm, carrying riders to the top in approximately 12 minutes. On-site facilities include a café serving breakfast wraps, gourmet coffee, and home-cooked lunches; a bike shop stocking spares, riding gear, and merchandise; toilets; and free car parking. Full-face helmet, gloves, and knee pads are mandatory. A waiver is required; riders under 16 must have a parent or guardian signature.

claimsNeedingHumanReview.issue: Confirmed by three sources (Visit Mid Wales official directory, iBikeRide, Mountain Biking UK). However, top100attractions.com lists a different number: 01654 701383. The 01691 prefix is for the Oswestry area (consistent with the registered office in Llanrhaeadr ym Mochnant), while 01654 is for Machynlleth (where the park is physically located). Both could plausibly be correct. Recommend calling both numbers or emailing the operator to confirm the current public enquiries number.
